name: Question 16
problem: Estimate $\sqrt{4.1}+\operatorname{ln}⁡(0.9)$ using a differential $\text{d}f$ of the function $f(x,y)=\sqrt{x}+\operatorname{ln}⁡y$ at the point $(4,1).$
worked_solution:
First, let's find the differential:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{d}f(x,y) & =(\frac{∂f}{∂x})\,\text{d}x+(\frac{∂f}{∂y})\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}x+\frac{1}{y}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

At the point $(4,1),$ the differential is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{d}f(x,y) & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{4}}\,\text{d}x+\frac{1}{1}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\,\text{d}x+1\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

So, if we move to the point $(4+Δx,1+Δy),$ then we can approximate the change in $f$ as

$$
Δf≈\frac{1}{4}\,Δx+1\,Δy
$$

Note that 

$$
\sqrt{4.1}+\operatorname{ln}⁡(0.9)=f(4.1,0.9),
$$

so we want to move to the point $(4.1,0.9).$

Moving from $(4,1)$ to $(4.1,0.9),$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Δx & =4.1-4=0.1, \\ Δy & =0.9-1=-0.1.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Δf & ≈\frac{1}{4}\cdot (0.1)+1(-0.1) \\  & ≈0.025-0.1 \\  & ≈-0.075.\end{aligned}
$$

This means that the value of $f$ decreases by about $0.075.$ Consequently, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(4.1,0.9) & ≈f(4,1)-0.075 \\ \sqrt{4.1}+\operatorname{ln}⁡(0.9) & ≈\sqrt{4}+\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)-0.075 \\  & ≈2-0.075 \\  & ≈1.925.\end{aligned}
$$

Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, let's find the differential:

df(x,y)=(∂f∂x)dx+(∂f∂y)dy=12xdx+1ydy.

At the point (4,1), the differential is

df(x,y)=124dx+11dy=14dx+1dy.

So, if we move to the point (4+Δx,1+Δy), then we can approximate the change in f as

Δf≈14Δx+1Δy

Note that 4.1+ln⁡(0.9)=f(4.1,0.9),

so we want to move to the point (4.1,0.9).

Moving from (4,1) to (4.1,0.9), we have

Δx=4.1−4=0.1,Δy=0.9−1=−0.1.

So, we have

Δf≈14⋅(0.1)+1(−0.1)≈0.025−0.1≈−0.075.

This means that the value of f decreases by about 0.075. Consequently, we have

f(4.1,0.9)≈f(4,1)−0.0754.1+ln⁡(0.9)≈4+ln⁡(1)−0.075≈2−0.075≈1.925.
